sessions.result:
`precisedelta()` now keeps the sign of a negative value, so `precisedelta(timedelta(seconds=-3661))` returns `'-1 hour, 1 minute and 1 second'`. The full suite passes (756 passed, 112 skipped), and so do the doctests in `src`. I didn't run the new tests against the base commit, so the fail-first check is reasoned rather than observed. The sign-keeping assertions would fail there because the old code returned the unsigned text.

I couldn't make a strong case against merging this, so I'm approving it. The full suite passes (756 passed, 112 skipped). The reproducing check fails on the base commit and passes here, and only `src/humanize/time.py` and `tests/test_time.py` changed.

**What holds up**
- The fix in `precisedelta()` handles negatives in one place: it renders the absolute value by calling itself, then adds a leading `-`.
